cim: Clemson University to launch three new degree programs in artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Clemson University to launch three new degree programs in artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Three new degree programs in artificial intelligence will launch at Clemson University in fall 2027 to prepare the next generation of leaders, innovators and entrepreneurs to shape the future of the rapidly advancing technology.

Students will have the opportunity to pursue bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral degrees through Clemson’s School of Computing.

The programs will be aimed at helping prepare the future workforce for careers in industries ranging from cybersecurity and advanced manufacturing to health care and finance.

J. Cole Smith, executive vice president for academic affairs and provost, said the new programs will strengthen Clemson’s commitment to delivering the nation’s No. 1 student experience while supporting its continued rise as a leading research university.

“Artificial intelligence is transforming industries, creating new opportunities and changing the skills employers need,” he said. “These programs will give students the skills to lead that transformation while creating new opportunities for research, discovery and innovation.”

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects strong demand for workers with AI-related skills, with employment expected to grow 15.8% for software developers, 19.7% for computer and information research scientists and 33.5% for data scientists.

Altogether, those occupations are projected to generate about 141,800 job openings annually, with employment growth of 18.1%, well above the national average.

O. Thompson Mefford, associate dean for undergraduate studies in the College of Engineering, Computing and Applied Sciences, said the new programs will prepare students to apply AI across a wide range of fields.

“Artificial intelligence is becoming part of nearly every industry, and we want our graduates to be ready to lead the way,” he said. “They will gain technical knowledge, hands-on experience and an understanding of how AI affects people. Those skills will help them solve problems, develop new ideas and make a meaningful impact.”

Brian Dean, C. Tycho Howle Director of Clemson University’s School of Computing, said the new degree programs will give students opportunities to explore artificial intelligence from multiple perspectives while developing skills that can be applied across a wide range of disciplines.

“Artificial intelligence is opening doors to careers and research opportunities that would have been difficult to imagine just a few years ago,” Dean said. “We want our students to have the knowledge, creativity and practical experience to make the most of those opportunities and help shape what comes next.”

All three degree programs will be based on Clemson’s main campus and taught in person. The new programs will expand opportunities for students, strengthen Clemson’s AI research capabilities and help meet growing workforce demands, said Anand Gramopadhye, the college’s dean.

Bachelor of Science: The interdisciplinary bachelor’s program will require 123 credit hours and combine programming, mathematics and statistics with courses in artificial intelligence, business, ethics and human-centered design. It is intended for students with a wide range of interests who want careers in computing, AI and related fields or who plan to pursue graduate study.

Master of Science: The 30-credit-hour master’s program will include six core courses and four electives covering advanced AI topics, with no thesis required. It is aimed at students who want to build on their undergraduate education in computing, engineering, science or other fields with a strong mathematical foundation.

Ph.D.: The doctoral program will require at least 70 credit hours for students entering with a bachelor’s degree or 40 credit hours for those entering with a master’s degree in a related field. It combines advanced coursework with original research leading to a dissertation. The program is designed for students seeking research careers in academia or industry who want to develop new AI technologies and applications.

The South Carolina Commission on Higher Education has approved all three degree programs, which are scheduled to begin in fall 2027.

Melissa Smith, the college’s associate dean of graduate studies, said the new programs will strengthen Clemson’s role in developing the talent and technology needed to support South Carolina’s growing economy.

“Artificial intelligence is creating tremendous opportunities for innovation across nearly every industry,” she said. “These programs will help us build a strong pipeline of talent, expand our research capabilities and work with industry partners to turn new ideas into solutions that benefit South Carolina and beyond.”

Interested students can contact Brian Dean at bcdean@clemson.edu for information.
